title: the WSG movement in waterborne vehicles
audit_label: R455 WSG waterborne vehicles pin audit
audit_comment: The waterborne vehicles slice pins Table 25 (the eight inland vessels - kayak through large barge - across length, width, the passenger-plus-gold capacity, the four large-scale miles-per-half-day and four small-scale feet-per-round rates, the encumbrance ranges with the large barge open 10000+, the startup and hull ranges, and the draughts) and the modifications to movement (the downstream add and upstream subtract of the current, the 20-to-30 wind band with the minus-1 and plus-2 steps per 10 mph, the 5 mph no-sail floor, the right-angle maximum sail, the into-wind 3-inch reduction to the 1-inch minimum, the two-turns-on one-turn-off max-oar exertion with the fatigued half speed and the forced one-turn exhaustion, and the shorthanded proportionate rowing per the 3-rowers large-rowboat example) (rules/wsgvessels.h, prefix wvb); census 379 -> 380.

banner.title: The WSG MOVEMENT IN WATERBORNE VEHICLES, R455: Table 25, the WATERBORNE VEHICLE CHARACTERISTICS of the eight inland vessels - kayak (length 8-12, width 2-3, capacity 1 + 1000, large move 18/24/12/14, small move 160/200/120/180, enc. 600-800, startup 1-2, hull 1-2, draught 1/4), small canoe (10-15, 2-3, 2 + 2500, 20/30/10/12, 160/200/120/180, 700-900, 1-2, 1-2, 1/4), small rowboat (8-12, 2-4, 2 + 2000, 16/24/12/14, 120/180/90/120, 700-1000, 1-3, 1-3, 1/2), coracle (10-15, 3-5, 2 + 2000, 12/18/6/8, 45/60/30/45, 900-1200, 1-3, 1-2, 1/2), large canoe (15-20, 2-3, 2 + 4000, 20/30/10/12, 120/180/90/120, 1000-1200, 1-3, 2-3, 1/3), large rowboat (15-20, 3-4, 4 + 4000, 16/24/8/10, 45/90/45/60, 1200-1600, 2-5, 2-4, 3/4), small barge (15-20, 8-12, 4 + 6000, 16/24/8/9, 45/60/30/45, 4000-6000, 2-6, 1-6, 3/4) and large barge (25-45, 12-20, 6 + 7500, 8/16/4/5, 30/60/20/30, 10000+, 5-10, 2-8, draught 1). Large move is miles per half-day under normal sail, maximum sail, normal oar and maximum oar; small move is feet per round under the same four. The modifications: if the water is moving the vessel drifts with the current at that speed - downstream the normal sail or normal oar rate ADDS the current, upstream the current is DEDUCTED and maximum sail or oar may be needed for headway. Normal sail assumes movement in the direction of the wind blowing between 20 and 30 miles per hour: subtract 1 inch (one mile per half-day or 10 feet per round) for each 10 mph of wind below 20, add 2 inches for each 10 mph above 30 - and a vessel cannot be successfully sailed if the wind is less than 5 miles per hour. Maximum sail applies when moving at RIGHT ANGLES to the wind, with the same wind-speed modifiers; a vessel sailed INTO the wind has its normal sail rate reduced by 3 inches per 10 mph of wind speed, to a minimum of 1 inch in any case. The maximum oar rate is extremely strenuous: a character must rest or row at the normal rate for one turn after two turns of such effort or risk fatigue - a fatigued oarsman can only propel the craft at HALF normal speed, and if forced to row at normal speed he becomes exhausted after one turn. A craft can be rowed by fewer characters than the capacity figure, but only at a PROPORTIONATE fraction of its movement rate - the printed example: three people rowing a large rowboat travel 6 miles in eight hours at normal oar (three-quarters of 8) or 45 feet per round at maximum oar (three-quarters of 60). All these rates and modifiers assume at least one character aboard with proficiency in boating. The rules cover only inland-waterway vessels - galleys, merchant ships and warships are out of scope. Census 379 -> 380.
banner.provenance: the WSG scan (archive.org item pdfy-B3Fz83tZ3TV7zOc8), printed p. 44 with the movement-modification prose continuing on p. 45; the user own copy OCR (pages 45-46) cross-checked against the archive djvu word layer (Guide_0044, Guide_0045) - the prose reads clean two-way, but the djvu TRUNCATES the printed Table 25 (only six of eight rows, the draught column garbled, the barge rows missing), so the grid was settled by TWO independent IIIF eye-reads of leaf $44, which agree with the OCR exactly on all eight rows and every cell, including the 10000+ open-ended encumbrance of the large barge.
banner.sentinel: Eight boats for the inland waters, from the one-man kayak to the 45-foot barge: four move rates apiece - sail and oar, normal and maximum - plus capacity, encumbrance, startup, hull and draught. Drift with the current, add it going down, lose it going up; sail best at right angles to a 20-to-30-mile wind, lose 3 inches rowing into it, none at all under 5; row hard for two turns, rest for one, or row short-handed at a fraction - three men in a large rowboat make 6 miles a half-day and 45 feet a round.

consts.name: wvbVesselCount
consts.comment: Table 25 lists eight waterborne vehicles: kayak, small canoe, small rowboat, coracle, large canoe, large rowboat, small barge and large barge.

consts.name: wvbWindBandMin
consts.comment: The normal sail rates assume the craft is moved in the direction of the wind, and that the wind is blowing between 20 and 30 miles per hour.

consts.name: wvbWindBandMax
consts.comment: The top of the assumed wind band for normal sail: 20 to 30 miles per hour.

consts.name: wvbWindLowStep
consts.comment: Subtract 1 inch (one mile per half-day or 10 feet per round) for each 10 miles per hour of wind speed less than 20.

consts.name: wvbWindHighStep
consts.comment: Add 2 inches for each 10 miles per hour of wind speed greater than 30.

consts.name: wvbInchPerHalfDayMiles
consts.comment: One inch of vessel movement is one mile per half-day of eight hours on the large scale.

consts.name: wvbInchPerRoundFt
consts.comment: One inch of vessel movement is 10 feet per round on the small scale.

consts.name: wvbMinSailWind
consts.comment: A vessel cannot be successfully sailed if the wind is less than 5 miles per hour.

consts.name: wvbIntoWindStep
consts.comment: A vessel being sailed into the wind has its normal sail rate reduced by 3 inches for each 10 miles per hour of wind speed.

consts.name: wvbIntoWindMinIn
consts.comment: The into-wind reduction bottoms out: the normal sail rate has a minimum of 1 inch (1 mile per eight hours or 10 feet per round) in any case.

consts.name: wvbMaxOarEffortTurns
consts.comment: Traveling at the maximum oar rate is considered extremely strenuous activity: the effort can be maintained for two turns before rest is required.

consts.name: wvbMaxOarRestTurns
consts.comment: After two turns of maximum-oar effort the character must rest, or simply row at the normal rate, for one turn, or run the risk of becoming fatigued and subsequently exhausted.

consts.name: wvbFatiguedSpeedDiv
consts.comment: An oarsman or paddler who becomes fatigued can only propel his craft at half normal speed until his condition is alleviated.

consts.name: wvbFatiguedExhaustTurns
consts.comment: If a fatigued oarsman is forced to continue rowing at normal speed, he will automatically become exhausted after one turn of such activity.

consts.name: wvbExRowers
consts.comment: The printed example: three people row a large rowboat, one fewer than the four listed under its capacity figure.

consts.name: wvbExNormalOarMiles
consts.comment: The printed example: three people rowing a large rowboat can only travel 6 miles in eight hours at the normal oar rate - three-quarters of the 8-mile figure.

consts.name: wvbExMaxOarFt
consts.comment: The printed example: the same three rowers travel 45 feet per round in small-scale movement under the maximum oar rate - three-quarters of the 60-foot figure.

bools.name: wvbInlandVesselsOnly
bools.comment: These rules are limited to vessels normally found on inland waterways, primarily lakes and rivers; galleys, merchant ships and warships are seagoing vessels and out of scope.

bools.name: wvbLoadDistributedEvenly
bools.comment: The capacity figures assume cargo and passengers are distributed evenly in or on the vessel; a rowboat loaded too heavily on one side will capsize fairly easily even under its limit.

bools.name: wvbMaxOarLowGainRationale
bools.comment: The maximum-oar figures are relatively low because the accelerated movement can only be maintained for short periods, so the gain in mileage over time is small.

bools.name: wvbDraughtHullDamageRisk
bools.comment: If a craft is operated in water the same depth as its draught figure, there may be a chance (at the DM discretion) of hull damage, particularly for a less sturdy type such as a kayak or coracle.

bools.name: wvbProficiencyAssumed
bools.comment: All the given movement rates and the modifiers in this section assume the presence on board of at least one character with proficiency in boating.

bools.name: wvbCurrentDrift
bools.comment: If the water is moving, a vessel will drift with the current at that speed.

bools.name: wvbCurrentAddsDownstream
bools.comment: If the craft is sailed or rowed while moving downstream, the normal sail or normal oar rate is added to the speed of the current to determine the actual movement rate.

bools.name: wvbCurrentSubtractsUpstream
bools.comment: The converse applies against the current: the speed of the water is deducted from the given movement rate, and maximum sail or maximum oar may be necessary to make headway.

bools.name: wvbSailAssumesWindDirection
bools.comment: The normal sail rates assume the craft is being moved in the direction of the wind.

bools.name: wvbNoSailBelowMinWind
bools.comment: A vessel cannot be successfully sailed if the wind is less than 5 miles per hour.

bools.name: wvbMaxSailRightAngles
bools.comment: The maximum sail rate applies if a vessel is moving at right angles to the wind, with the same wind-speed modifiers for below 20 or above 30 miles per hour.

bools.name: wvbIntoWindReduced
bools.comment: A vessel being sailed into the wind has its normal sail rate reduced by 3 inches per 10 miles per hour of wind speed, to a minimum of 1 inch in any case.

bools.name: wvbMaxOarStrenuous
bools.comment: Traveling at the maximum oar rate is considered extremely strenuous activity for any character engaged in propelling the craft.

bools.name: wvbFatiguedHalfSpeed
bools.comment: A fatigued oarsman or paddler can only propel his craft at half normal speed until his condition is alleviated.

bools.name: wvbFatiguedForcedExhaust
bools.comment: If a fatigued oarsman is forced to continue rowing at normal speed, he will automatically become exhausted after one turn of such activity.

bools.name: wvbShorthandedProportional
bools.comment: A craft can be rowed or paddled by fewer characters than the capacity figure, but the vessel can only be moved at a proportionate fraction of its movement rate.
